searchText: Yeah I don’t think IndexedAttestation is correct I think it arose from some miscommunication that can probably be attributed to me I’m all for replacing IndexedAttestation with Attestation Personally, I prefer get an Attestation and send back an attestation (not using AttestationData from node to validator) Just checked our implementations, our `get` is returning `AttestationData` and `post` is accepting `Attestation` The trade off here is validator has to keep track of it's index for using `AttestationData` so it knows how to construct its aggregation bit field I'm happy with using `Attestation` both ways, I dont feel too strongly about either Yeah I don't feel to strongly either. I was thinking that if we had `Attestation` both ways and the validator always just added their signature to the aggregate, then the node could possibly send a pre-aggregated `Attestation` (one with some aggregation bits set to true). I'm just not sure on the BLS specifics of sending an empty (0) signature and having the validator add on top of it Yea I agree. Returning `Attestation` feels more scalable. We dont want validators to worry about aggregating signatures down the line 👍 I think <@535705896224030720> had it on his todo list to update that minimal validator swagger sorry that it caught you out <@545555441518772225> To keep the validator thin on logic and still remove the indexed dependency, the validator could send back the attestationdata, a signature, and their index. The (smarter) node could then construct the full attestation from the pieces and broadcast Wouldn't the validator logic be even thinner if it was just `Attestation`both ways? The validator has to know their index within the attestation. Aah i see with the custody bit already set I mean aggregation bit yeah, the request for an attestation would need to specify `custody_bit`, then the node could return the `Attestation` with the bitfields already configured It also means that the validator client (after signing) ends up with a fully-self contained attestation that could be broadcast to multiple nodes easily `get_attestation_from_node(epoch, validator_index, custody_bit)` -- something like that Increases size of transfer by 1024 bytes both ways in worst case (4096 validators in committee) True. Good point True It's a local RPC though, 1kb is probably fine IMO Yeah, think so too. The advantage of having fully constructed an attestation to do whatever you want with is the winning point i think Heading to dinner. Talk soon Yea this also keeps the validator logic at a very minimal, just retrieve, sign and submit Talk to ya later! Bon appetit! Yeah agreed with the above. We chose to use `IndexedAttestation` in the RPC spec because we didn't want the validator to have to calculate the size of the committee bit fields, but in retrospect this doesn't make much sense. I am working on an update to this spec, which will include sending/receiving just an `Attestation`, rather than an `IndexedAttestation`, and this will be reflected in our implementation soon. I hate timezones, started and missed the party 😂 I like sending attestation back and forth. Would be nice in future to raise those issues as we encounter them and not just silently diverge from agreed API 😛 Definitely. It was only a couple of days ago that we resolved this conversation ourselves, which is why we hadn't raised it yet. I will submit a PR on the eth2.0-APIs repo soon, alongisde our updated API spec.

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: Yeah I don’t think IndexedAttestation is correct

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: I think it arose from some miscommunication that can probably be attributed to me

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: I’m all for replacing IndexedAttestation with Attestation

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: Personally, I prefer get an Attestation and send back an attestation (not using AttestationData from node to validator)

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Just checked our implementations, our `get` is returning `AttestationData` and `post` is accepting `Attestation`

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: The trade off here is validator has to keep track of it's index for using `AttestationData` so it knows how to construct its aggregation bit field

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: I'm happy with using `Attestation` both ways, I dont feel too strongly about either

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
Yeah I don't feel to strongly either.

I was thinking that if we had `Attestation` both ways and the validator always just added their signature to the aggregate, then the node could possibly send a pre-aggregated `Attestation` (one with some aggregation bits set to true).

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: I'm just not sure on the BLS specifics of sending an empty (0) signature and having the validator add on top of it

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Yea I agree.  Returning `Attestation` feels more scalable. We dont want validators to worry about aggregating signatures down the line 👍

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: I think <@535705896224030720> had it on his todo list to update that minimal validator swagger

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: sorry that it caught you out <@545555441518772225>

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: To keep the validator thin on logic and still remove the indexed dependency, the validator could send back the attestationdata, a signature, and their index. The (smarter) node could then construct the full attestation from the pieces and broadcast

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: Wouldn't the validator logic be even thinner if it was just `Attestation`both ways?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: The validator has to know their index within the attestation.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: Aah i see with the custody bit already set

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I mean aggregation bit

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: yeah, the request for an attestation would need to specify `custody_bit`, then the node could return the `Attestation` with the bitfields already configured

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: It also means that the validator client (after signing) ends up with a fully-self contained attestation that could be broadcast to multiple nodes easily

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: `get_attestation_from_node(epoch, validator_index, custody_bit)` -- something like that

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: Increases size of transfer by 1024 bytes both ways in worst case (4096 validators in committee)

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: True. Good point

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: True

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: It's a local RPC though, 1kb is probably fine IMO

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: Yeah, think so too. The advantage of having fully constructed an attestation to do whatever you want with is the winning point i think

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: Heading to dinner. Talk soon

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Yea this also keeps the validator logic at a very minimal, just retrieve, sign and submit

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Talk to ya later!

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: Bon appetit!

excerpts.author: spble
excerpts.content:
Yeah agreed with the above.
We chose to use `IndexedAttestation` in the RPC spec because we didn't want the validator to have to calculate the size of the committee bit fields, but in retrospect this doesn't make much sense. I am working on an update to this spec, which will include sending/receiving just an `Attestation`, rather than an `IndexedAttestation`, and this will be reflected in our implementation soon.
